title: Phase-Resolved Hydraulic Flux Seam

invariants.evidence: Adds one generic result/view seam to the single SWAP5 kernel architecture; no use-case-specific SWAP implementation.
Production modules contain no file, path, parsing or format dependency.
Face transport is explicit result/view data and is not mixed into immutable parameters, forcing, numerical policy or committed physical state.
No persistent per-column state is added; allocatable face arrays exist only in the derived candidate result view.
Reference numerical residual/source/sink data remain in the existing worker-owned workspace; no scratch is moved into column state.
The contract permits alternative internal storage/layouts, but EB-I03 does not benchmark batched/SoA/SIMD materialization or cache behavior.
The view is explicitly candidate/trial scoped and retry results fail closed, but end-to-end runtime commit/rollback publication is intentionally deferred and is not qualified here.
The derived view mutates no committed state and can be recomputed from the same candidate solve data; existing warm-start behavior is untouched.
Transport is tied to generic solver step_duration; no calendar day/month/year boundary is assumed. cm/day is the existing rate unit, not a scheduling assumption.
No coupling-window size, midnight boundary or fixed reporting interval is encoded.
The seam provides conservation-relevant candidate transport for future coupling/runtime use, but runtime/coupler publication is not part of EB-I03.
Existing top/bottom groundwater exchange fluxes are not altered; the reconstructed bottom face is compared against the existing published bottom flux and inconsistency remains diagnostic.
EB-I03 preserves the final continuity residual explicitly and never forces it to zero. It does not modify hydraulic state, accepted fluxes or the existing mass-balance authority.
No groundwater response tangent or sensitivity contract is changed or added.
The view requires no extra full SWAP solve or predictor/corrector run; it is derived from an already converged candidate solve.
No persistent heavy solver instance is added, but hundred-thousand-column allocation/throughput behavior is not qualified in this workunit.
The view is per logical SWAP column. Tile fractions and MODFLOW-cell aggregation remain outside the hydraulic process contract.
No deep-vadose component behavior is changed.
No transition between deep-vadose and direct groundwater coupling is changed.

The consumer-facing phase-flux view is solver-independent; the reference-Richards reconstruction is isolated in an adapter and other soil-water solvers may implement the same logical result independently.
Existing Richards physics and discrete residual algebra are reused without duplication or alteration; the new adapter only materializes conservation-relevant result data.
Consumers depend on mod_soil_water_phase_flux_view rather than HeadCalc internals. Reference-specific workspace access is confined to the adapter producer.
No physical option is changed by numerical policy. Vapor/macropore absence is represented as unavailable coverage rather than silently changing physics.
The derived replay is O(n), but bounded-cost behavior for difficult columns and full MultiSWAP throughput are not benchmarked or qualified here.
The admitted reference Richards route remains byte-identical and available; EB-I03 does not replace or alter reference-mode physics.
The view publishes phase-coverage flags, continuity residuals and bottom consistency diagnostics, but runtime-wide diagnostic aggregation/reporting is deferred.
No face arrays are added to persistent state. Allocation occurs only when the optional producer is invoked for a requested candidate result.
System composition, energy-ledger transfer and tile/coupler aggregation remain runtime/coupler responsibilities; EB-I03 is a column-local process-result seam.
No .swp input, filesystem, midnight, one-day or mandatory-MODFLOW assumption is present.
EB-I03 is explicitly assessed against all 30 SWAP core architecture invariants in this audit.

hard_nonclaims: No full SWAP5 energy balance is qualified.
No vapor flux is invented or treated as covered zero transport.
No freeze/thaw phase transport is qualified.
No macropore path-resolved transport is qualified.
q*dt is only the backward-Euler interval-equivalent amount represented by the admitted discrete solve, not a higher-order continuous-time flux integral.
Candidate phase-flux results are not yet transactionally transferred into a committed runtime or energy ledger.
Large-batch MultiSWAP throughput and bounded-cost behavior are not qualified.
Independent verification and canonical admission are not claimed.
